domain: V178 hosting comparison - confidential VM candidates (owner directive: ANNULATION V178.2 / NOUVEAU VPS CONFIDENTIEL §7)
method: WebSearch summaries + WebFetch of 2 OVHcloud OCCAM pages; generic queries; no account, no purchase, no instance creation, no spend. Prices: official where stated, otherwise third-party trackers (marked). Regional availability changes often - re-check live pages before any decision. Items marked UNVERIFIED or general-knowledge are not sourced in this run.
workloadAssumption: 8-16 vCPU / 32-64 GB RAM, CPU-only LLM (Ollama/llama.cpp 3-7B quantized) + embeddings; EU region; independently verifiable attestation + key release.

signals.title: Google Cloud Confidential VM - Intel TDX on C3 (Sapphire Rapids), GA; europe-west4 and europe-west9 zones
signals.claim: TDX on c3-standard-* GA since Sept 2024; EU zones listed: europe-west4-a/b/c (Netherlands) and europe-west9-a (Paris) per most recent localized copy (older copies list only europe-west4-a/b). c3-standard-*-lssd TDX GA 2026-09-02 (EU zones not shown). TDX on c4-standard-* in Preview since 2026-07-31. Limits: no reservations; local SSD machine types not supported (except -lssd variant); maintenance notification 7 days on C3 TDX; up to 192 vCPUs. AMX enabled by default on all C3 incl. Confidential VMs. GPU-CVM: a3-highgpu-1g (H100) with NVIDIA CC in europe-west4-c; g4-standard-48 TDX in europe-west4-b/c.

attestation.whatIsAttested: TDX quote: MRTD (Google-built OVMF/TDVF firmware) + RTMRs (boot chain), report data = your nonce; plus vTPM-based measured boot for OS.
attestation.signedBy: Intel (quote signed by TD Quoting Enclave key chaining to Intel root via PCS collateral); firmware measurement endorsed by Google (signed launch endorsement).
attestation.independentVerification: YES for hardware genuineness: Google codelab verifies the raw TDX quote with go-tdx-guest 'check' against Intel PCS collateral + CRL, nonce check, then 'gcetcbendorsement tdx validate' for Google-endorsed firmware, 'gceprovenance verify' for host provenance. You still trust Google's firmware endorsement for what MRTD means (or reproduce firmware build - not verified as possible). Alternative: Google Cloud Attestation service returns token (provider-operated verifier).

signals.keyRelease: Options: (a) self-hosted KMS off-Google that verifies the raw TDX quote then releases keys (fully provider-independent); (b) Google Cloud Attestation token + Cloud KMS via Workload Identity Pool (Confidential Space; STET uses Confidential Space token as attestation evidence for KEK in Cloud KMS); (c) Cloud EKM keeps keys with an external key manager - EKM + Confidential Space attestation integration NOT confirmed in this run.
signals.diskBootIntegrity: Measured boot via vTPM/RTMR; Confidential Hyperdisk billed separately (pricing page). Snapshot behaviour for CVM disks NOT found in this run.

indicativePrice.value: TDX surcharge on-demand: $0.0033982/vCPU-h + $0.0004555/GiB-h -> c3-standard-8 (8 vCPU/32 GB) adds ~$0.042/h (~$31/month at 730h). Base c3-standard-8 europe-west4 price NOT retrieved.

signals.sla: Compute Engine single-instance SLA >=99.9% (most families, per SLA page snapshots) - confirm for C3/CVM. Source: https://cloud.google.com/compute/sla
signals.llmFeasibility: Best CPU fit among GCP CVMs: Sapphire Rapids AVX-512 + AMX; llama.cpp has AMX kernels for Q4_0/Q4_1/Q8_0 when built with GGML_NATIVE on AMX host (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/8998). AMX speedup in llama.cpp NOT measured; known detection issues reported.
signals.risks: US-HQ provider (CLOUD Act context, H-LEGAL-1); TDX advisories (INTEL-SA-01419/01421/01520) require TCB policy; no reservations; trust in Google firmware endorsement.

signals.title: OVHcloud Bare Metal + OCCAM attestation service - ALPHA (no SLA, free during Alpha), EU only
signals.claim: OCCAM (OVHcloud Labs) = Confidential Computing Attestation Service, status ALPHA / early access (Labs release date 2026-11-18; roadmap issue #556 opened 2026-11-24, 'In progress', 'Partially released'); Beta and GA announced without dates or pricing. Customer runs its own Confidential VM (SEV-SNP or TDX) on an OVHcloud dedicated server (Advance, Scale, High Grade). Verified hardware per Labs page: AMD SEV-SNP Turin (EPYC 9005) and Genoa (EPYC 9004), single-socket; Intel TDX Xeon 6 (Granite Rapids). Roadmap issue additionally lists TDX on 5th-gen Xeon (Emerald Rapids) single-socket, while Labs page says 5th gen 'not yet verified' (CONFLICT). Host OS: Ubuntu 26.04 or Proxmox VE 9. GPU: TDX VM with 8x NVIDIA B300 verified, but GPU servers not open in Alpha.

attestation.whatIsAttested: The Confidential VM (not the host OS): firmware, kernel, initrd, boot command line; TDX: MRTD + RTMR0-2.
attestation.signedBy: Hardware report signed by AMD/Intel (chained to vendor roots); OCCAM result signed EAT/ES256 with a key bound to the OCCAM verifier's own SEV-SNP attestation report.
attestation.independentVerification: YES (claimed): results verifiable offline with published signer evidence; transparency page lets users recompute the verifier's measurement from published sources. Because the customer controls the bare-metal host and VM image, raw SNP reports / TDX quotes can also be verified by a self-hosted verifier (inference). Strict third-party verification of AMD reports requires SEV firmware >= 1.58.6.

signals.keyRelease: Built-in: root and data disk keys (LUKS2 + dm-verity) released only if measurement matches a customer-signed policy list; key can be split in two with one share held outside OCCAM; revocation of approved measurements refused while a running server uses it.
signals.diskBootIntegrity: LUKS2 + dm-verity tied to attested measurement (claimed).

indicativePrice.value: OCCAM: free during Alpha. Server: Advance-1 2026 (EPYC 4245P) EUR 104.99 ex-VAT/month; Advance-2 2024 (EPYC 4344P, 8c/16t) EUR 124.99; Advance-3 2024 (EPYC 4464P, 12c) EUR 199.99 - BUT OCCAM-verified CPUs are EPYC 9004/9005 / Xeon 6; whether these EPYC 4004/4005 Advance models support SEV-SNP or OCCAM is NOT verified. RISE-XL EPYC 9455 (Turin, 48c, 128 GB) $479.99/month 'soon available' (US page; RISE not in OCCAM range list).

signals.sla: OCCAM: NO SLA (Alpha). Dedicated server SLA not collected.
signals.llmFeasibility: Genoa/Turin (Zen 4/5) have AVX-512 (general knowledge - UNVERIFIED here); Xeon 6 has AMX (general knowledge). AMD claims llama.cpp + ZenDNN up to 4.5x prompt processing on EPYC (vendor claim): https://www.amd.com/en/developer/resources/technical-articles/2026/llama-cpp-on-amd-epyc.html. Full server = all cores/RAM dedicated -> best perf/EUR.
signals.hardware: OVHcloud dedicated server with EPYC 9004/9005 single-socket or Xeon 6 (OCCAM-verified list)
signals.risks: ALPHA: features may change, no SLA, limited CPU/host coverage, dual-socket AMD not measured, 'end-to-end confidential inference not yet available'; customer operates the hypervisor (Ubuntu 26.04/Proxmox) = more ops work; OVHcloud keeps physical access + BMC/BIOS (BadRAM/Battering RAM and CVE-2026-0462-class BIOS+PCIe attacks are physical/firmware-level); OVHcloud is EU-HQ (French) but has US subsidiary (CLOUD Act reach depends on control - legal question).

signals.title: Relevance of published CVM attacks to each candidate
signals.claim: Software/hypervisor-level attacks (CacheWarp CVE-2023-20592, Heracles, TDX advisories INTEL-SA-01419) are mitigated by firmware/microcode -> require attestation policy pinning minimum TCB (SNP firmware >=1.58.6 noted by OCCAM for strict verification). Physical attacks (BadRAM CVE-2024-21944, Battering RAM 2025) need datacentre access -> residual provider-insider risk on ALL candidates. CVE-2026-0462 / AMD-SB-3059 (hypervisor + BIOS + PCIe device -> forged measurements; secondary source) is most relevant where the provider controls BIOS: all candidates, incl. OVH bare metal (provider controls BMC/BIOS).
signals.risks: No candidate yields 'provider cannot access data' in absolute terms; claim must be 'protected against hypervisor/software access under the vendor threat model, residual physical/firmware risk'.

signals.title: US CLOUD Act: US-jurisdiction providers can be compelled to produce data they control regardless of storage location; Act is 'encryption neutral'
signals.claim: DOJ white paper (Apr 2019): CLOUD Act makes explicit that a provider subject to US jurisdiction can be required to produce data it controls regardless of where stored; it did not alter jurisdiction or add authority to compel decryption ('encryption neutral'). => Applies as legal context to Google Cloud and Azure (US parents); for EU-HQ providers with US affiliates (OVHcloud, IONOS) exposure depends on jurisdiction/control - legal analysis required. Technical relevance: if keys are held only by the customer (attestation-gated, off-provider KMS) the provider cannot produce plaintext it does not control (inference, not legal advice).
signals.risks: Not legal advice; executive agreements since 2019 not reviewed.

signals.title: Residency/sovereignty offerings: Microsoft EU Data Boundary (completed Feb 2025), Google Cloud Data Boundary / Sovereign Controls by Partners / Google Cloud Dedicated (S3NS, T-Systems)
signals.claim: Microsoft EU Data Boundary completed phase 3 (Feb 2025): customer data and support data stored/processed in EU/EFTA. Google: Data Boundary = software controls (residency, access, encryption) on public cloud; Sovereign Controls by Partners; Google Cloud Dedicated operated by independent regional operators (S3NS France, T-Systems Germany). These are residency/operational controls, not immunity from US law for the US-operated tiers.
signals.risks: Interaction between Assured Workloads EU controls and Confidential VM availability per zone NOT checked.

signals.title: CPU LLM inference feasibility by CPU generation (llama.cpp/Ollama)
signals.claim: llama.cpp includes AMX kernels (Q4_0/Q4_1/Q8_0) used when built natively on AMX hardware (PR #8998); Google enables AMX on all C3 incl. Confidential VMs; Intel guidance: Q8_0-style quants align best with VNNI/AMX; AMD claims llama.cpp+ZenDNN up to 4.5x prompt processing on EPYC (vendor claim). No measured CVM-vs-non-CVM LLM overhead found in this run. Memory bandwidth (not ISA) usually bounds token generation - more channels on server CPUs help (general knowledge).

recommendations.bestFitIndependentAttestationKeyReleaseE: Production-grade today: Google Cloud Intel TDX on C3 in europe-west9 (Paris) or europe-west4 - GA, independently verifiable raw quote against Intel PCS, AMX for CPU LLM, small public surcharge; pair with a self-hosted, off-provider KMS that verifies the quote before releasing tenant keys (avoids dependence on Google Attestation/Cloud KMS). Caveat: US-HQ provider (CLOUD Act legal context) - mitigated technically only by customer-held keys + attestation, not legally.
recommendations.bestSovereigntyAndCostIfAlphaAcceptable: OVHcloud bare metal + OCCAM: strongest design fit (EU-HQ, customer-controlled host and image, offline-verifiable signed results, built-in attested LUKS key release with split share, dedicated cores at bare-metal prices) but ALPHA with no SLA and limited CPU list - suitable for a pilot/PoC on non-production data, not for client production until Beta/GA.
recommendations.azure: Viable but weakest on 'independent' attestation (closed paravisor; SKR bound to MAA) and pricier at 16 vCPU per third-party trackers.
recommendations.gcpSnp: Works in Frankfurt, but Milan (AVX2) is the weakest CPU for LLM; prefer TDX/C3.
recommendations.followUps: Before any decision (no spend now): confirm live EU zone lists, base C3 price in europe-west9, which OVHcloud Advance/Scale SKUs carry EPYC 9004/9005 or Xeon 6 with SEV-SNP/TDX enabled, IONOS price, DPAs (Microsoft/OVHcloud/IONOS), and run an ODG llama.cpp benchmark inside a CVM.
